_comment: Documented differences of WingtipToys' operations suite (corpora/regression/wt.operations.scenario.json): differences that are not defects of the conversion, each with its reason. snapshot: a regular expression on the snapshot's name; match: one on each problem line ParityTest reports; platforms: where it applies (none: everywhere); check same-exception: only for two error pages of the same path, status and exception type. A snapshot all of whose problems match is 'allowed', not 'different'.

allowed.reason: message wording: the original's error pages are in the Japanese language pack of .NET Framework (Microsoft's texts of System.Web and mscorlib); the converted application's System.Web texts are FrameworkOnCore's own Japanese translation (Microsoft's are not redistributable: translations/ja), the .NET 10 runtime's exception messages are English (.NET has no localized runtime messages), and on Linux SQL Server's messages are the container's (English). Same page, status and exception type.

TLS: the original targets 4.5.2 (httpRuntime targetFramework), whose ServicePointManager default is SSL 3.0 / TLS 1.0; PayPal's sandbox refuses those, so its HttpWebRequest never connects and the page fails with ProtocolViolationException (500). .NET 10 uses the system's TLS 1.2/1.3: PayPal answers (10002 Security header is not valid, the sample's placeholder credentials) and the application redirects to CheckoutError as its code intends. Confirmed with .NET Framework's client: TLS 1.0 'Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel', TLS 1.2 200.

allowed.match: ^(本文テキスト|  (正解|実測)側にのみある行).*(/Content/css|/bundles/MsAjaxJs|/bundles/WebFormsJs)
allowed.reason: minifier version: the original's bundles are minified by WebGrease 1.5.2 (its embedded Microsoft Ajax Minifier); FrameworkOnCore's System.Web.Optimization uses the open-source WebGrease port (WebFormsForCore.WebGrease, a later Ajax Minifier). The same files, the same status and type; the minified text differs in variable naming and order, a space in '@media(...) and (...)', 'typeof event' for 'typeof window.event', a Debug.writeln call kept: equivalent in browsers (the pages' scripts work: every postback and validation step matches).

allowed.match: ^(本文テキスト|  (正解|実測)側にのみある行)
allowed.reason: IIS's own detailed error page is a simple page in FrameworkOnCore (the user's decision when httpErrors was made IIS-compatible, README 'httpErrors を IIS 互換で実装した'): the same status, substatus and title, the requested URL and physical path; not IIS's 'Most likely causes', module, handler, logon lines.

allowed.match: ^(本文テキスト|  (正解|実測)側にのみある行|テーブル1 )
allowed.reason: ELMAH lists the run's errors with their messages: the wording of the messages (as above), and one row more on the original - the ProtocolViolationException of PayPal's call (TLS, as above). The same codes and types otherwise, in the same order.

Request.IsLocal (the test's environment): the golden was recorded from IIS's own machine; the Linux container is reached through Docker's port forwarding, so the application sees the client as Docker's gateway (W3C log: c-ip 172.18.0.1, s-ip 172.18.0.3) and Request.IsLocal is false: ErrorPage.aspx leaves out its local-only details and ELMAH (allowRemoteAccess=false) answers 403. Requested from inside the container (127.0.0.1) the page shows the details and ELMAH answers 200. The same cause as the 8-step scenario's error-page on Linux.
